judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text runs an assignment prohibition into an unrelated 'unless cancelled, shall cover the insured's legal representative for the unexpired portion' clause, so the sentence as written does not parse.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the policy addresses assignment; the cancellation cross-reference points to Condition 12 (c055) but no contradiction emerges.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'other valid and collectible insurance ... whether or not described in the Schedule of Underlying Insurance' with a pro-rata contribution proviso is a dense escape/excess clause of the type courts frequently unpick.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with the Retained Limit definition (c034), which already counts 'any other underlying insurance collectible by the insured', and with the Overlap Endorsement (c106) on inter-insurer disputes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The apportionment waterfall is detailed but the OCR-mangled ordering of reimbursements could be read more than one way.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Wisconsin Amendatory Endorsement (c071) adds a made-whole rule that reverses the priority stated here, so the two must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'notice to or knowledge of any agent ... shall not effect a waiver' and 'changed only by endorsement' is a clear anti-waiver formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is squarely contradicted by the Wisconsin Amendatory Endorsement's CHANGES provision (c072), which makes an agent's knowledge the company's knowledge and bars avoidance on that ground.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The notice period reads 'not less than thirty (20) days', an internal numeric mismatch on the face of the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conflicts with the Wisconsin Cancellation Endorsement's 10-day periods (c065-c067) and with General Amendatory Endorsement No. 3's 60-day promise (c092).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'warranted ... shall be maintained in force' followed by a deeming rule if the insured fails to do so is a warranty whose consequences are contested; the 30-day exhaustion notice adds a second condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The deeming rule sits awkwardly with the drop-down clause (c009) and Loss Payable (c048), and the Wisconsin Declarations endorsement (c073) restricts the effect of breached warranties.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except insofar as coverage is available to the insured in the underlying insurance listed' is grammatically incomplete (listed where?) and 'liability assumed ... under any contract or agreement' is itself a much-litigated phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its following-form carve-out depends on underlying policies described only in Item 7, and it cuts against the insured-status limb keyed to written contracts to provide insurance (c029/c024).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It refers to the 'self insured retention listed in Item 7' when the SIR is stated in Item 4 and Item 7 is the schedule of underlying insurance — a cross-reference error inside a clause that strips mental injury, anguish and shock from Personal Injury.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directly cuts down the Personal Injury definition (c035), which expressly includes shock, mental anguish, false arrest, libel and privacy, and its 'except insofar as' proviso depends on the underlying schedule; this is the sharpest coverage conflict in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'initiated, alleged or caused to be brought about by a Named Insured ... against any other Named Insured' is broad and its trigger ('caused to be brought about') is hard to bound.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: With a dozen Named Insureds added by c085, c115, c117 and c120 and a separate class of 'additional insureds' under c088, whether a claimant is a Named Insured becomes a whole-instrument question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'if this policy applies to professional liability' is a conditional whose antecedent the policy itself does not settle.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Professional Services Exclusion (c082) removes professional health care services, yet this carve-out and the Aggregate Limits Endorsement (c084) assume professional liability cover exists.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence disapplying the endorsement to intrafamily automobile liability; narrow and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the omnibus automobile insured clause (c022) and the Item 7 auto policy; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It deletes and replaces an execution clause; nothing substantive to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to 'Form UML-002 (4/91)' while the policy form is UML 002 (1/91), a minor cross-reference slip with no coverage consequence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two alternative modes of cancellation by the insured (surrender or mailed notice) run together without an 'or', but the sense is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the first limb of Condition 12 (c055) and coexists with Item 6's short-rate minimum premium; substantially consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare lead-in sentence with no operative content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It introduces (a)-(e) which themselves conflict with c055 and c092, but the lead-in adds nothing of its own.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 10-day period and the 60-day/renewal conditions are numerically definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: General Amendatory Endorsement No. 3 (c092) promises 60 days' notice on any cancellation, contradicting this 10-day rule, as does Condition 12's 30 days (c055).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Non-payment cancellation on 10 days' notice is stated precisely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conflicts with the 60-day notice promised by c092 and interacts with the Pay Plan Endorsement's past-due rule (c098).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Substantial change in the risk assumed' and 'Substantial breaches of contractual duties, conditions or warranties' are evaluative standards with no defined boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 10-day notice again clashes with c092's 60-day promise, and the 'breach of warranty' ground sits against the Wisconsin Declarations endorsement (c073) limiting the effect of breached warranties.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence begins 'in addition to the right ... and provided that if this policy is written without a fixed expiration date', an awkward construction, but the mechanism is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The declared policy period is a fixed one-year term (03/01/1996 to 03/01/1997), so this paragraph has no field of operation under this policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'a right te to renewal' contains a stray duplication, and the entitlement 'on the terms then being applied by the Company to similar risks' is open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 60-day non-renewal notice matches c092, so the endorsements agree here even as they diverge on cancellation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first paragraph makes full compliance with all terms a condition precedent to any action while the second says any person or organization is entitled to recover to the extent of the insurance afforded — two sentences pulling opposite ways.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly deletes and replaces Condition 6 (c049) and repeats the bankruptcy rule of Condition 7 (c050); the compliance condition also interacts with the Wisconsin Declarations endorsement (c073).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'only after the insured has been fully compensated for damages' is a made-whole rule stated in one clean sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reverses the reimbursement priority set out in Condition 10 (c053), which the endorsement amends by addition rather than deletion, leaving the order of recovery arguable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The imputation rule is stated in absolute terms, but 'in the course of his dealings as an agent' has a soft boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts Condition 11 (c054), which says notice to or knowledge of any agent shall not effect a waiver or estop the company.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Statutory language reproduced; 'material', 'increases the risk' and 'contributes to the loss' are statutory standards rather than drafting defects.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It materially qualifies the warranty in c056, the notice condition in c046 and the condition precedent in c070, so its relationship with those is contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any insured subject of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act' is garbled ('subject of' for 'subject to'), but the exclusion's target is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision grants fiduciary or benefit-plan cover; nothing to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (b), 'property used by any Insured hereunder', is extremely broad and could swallow much third-party property damage cover.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states a wider version of the base policy's care-custody-control exclusion (c024), which is qualified by 'to the extent the insured is under contract to provide insurance', so the two differ in scope.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'directors and officers are excluded from this contract for liability arising out of wrongful acts' is loosely drafted — it excludes persons rather than claims.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Insured status is granted to executive officers and directors by the Insured definition (c021), and the carve-out in c078 restores most heads of cover, so the exclusion's residual field is unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'or any other matter claimed against them solely by reason of their being directors or officers' is a general catch-all after a specific list, and 'the company' is ambiguous as between insurer and insured entity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with c078's carve-out the definition may have almost nothing left to bite on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A carve-out for personal injury, bodily injury, property damage, hospital professional liability and advertisers liability restores essentially every head of coverage the policy grants.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because the policy insures only personal injury, property damage and advertising liability (c002), this carve-out arguably nullifies the D&O exclusion (c076) entirely, and it also assumes hospital professional liability cover that c082 excludes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence removing all discrimination injury from personal injury; blunt but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It squarely contradicts limb (5) of the Personal Injury definition (c035), which expressly includes racial or religious discrimination, and overlaps with the Personal Injury Endorsement (c058).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The copy is heavily degraded, but the exclusion sweeps in 'mental anguish and mental injury at any time' arising from manufacture, mining, use of or exposure to asbestos — a broad, list-plus-catch-all structure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its removal of mental injury overlaps with c058 and c035; otherwise it stands alone.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A no-defence provision whose text is partly illegible; the reach of 'resulting from or in any way' cannot be fixed from the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It negates the supplementary-payments defence duty (c003-c004) for asbestos claims, which is a deliberate override rather than an inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: For a hospital umbrella policy, an exclusion of 'injury to any person arising out of the rendering of or failure to render ... professional health care services' plus a peer-review limb is the central scope question, and 'in connection with such services' is open-textured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cannot be easily reconciled with the Aggregate Limits Endorsement's 'any professional liability hazard' (c084), the Cross Suits professional carve-out (c060), the Contingent Excess Medical Malpractice endorsement (c100-c104) or the professional liability limits endorsement (c121).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out turns entirely on whether an entity or individual is 'subject to the Wisconsin Patients Compensation Fund', a status term the policy never defines and which can be read as of the claim or of the policy inception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with c100-c102, which use a different formula ('defined by Wisconsin Statute 655.001 as a health care provider') and with c104, which disapplies form 035 in contingency cases, producing overlapping and inconsistent tests.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It adds 'or any professional liability hazard' to the aggregate proviso without defining that term, whereas 'products hazard' and 'completed operations hazard' are both defined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes professional liability coverage that the Professional Services Exclusion (c082) removes, and the aggregate figure it invokes is itself changed by Endorsement No. 4 (c109).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of entities followed by an express denial of automatic coverage for newly acquired entities invites expressio unius arguments about unlisted affiliates.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Named Insured definition (c020) automatically includes subsidiaries and controlled organisations, and later endorsements (c115, c117, c119, c120) add campuses and change the parent's name, so the list and the definition pull apart.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single deeming rule for notice; clear on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with the first-named-insured cancellation rule in Condition 12 (c055) and the 60-day notice in c092, which govern content rather than addressee.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure attachment boilerplate with no operative content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'unless otherwise stated herein' formula is consistent with the endorsement's stated effective date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'only with respect to their interest in the operations of the Named Insured' is a vague limitation — 'interest in the operations' has no ascertainable boundary, and the schedule's 'as their interest may appear' entries compound it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It creates a class of 'additional insureds' distinct from the 'Named Insureds' of c085, which matters directly for the Cross Suits Endorsement (c059) and the Insured definition (c031).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the endorsement it introduces (c090).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'but only as respects Med-Health Financial Services' is a precise limitation on the attached form.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The exclusion form itself (c099) is worded generally as to 'the Insured', so the endorsement's limitation and the form's own wording differ in reach.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the operative sentence it introduces (c092).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One short sentence promising 60 days' written notice; the words themselves are plain, though 'the insured' does not identify which insured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts Condition 12's 30-day notice (c055) and every limb of the Wisconsin Cancellation Endorsement's 10-day notices (c065, c066, c067), a direct clash between operative provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It replaces 'the exclusion relating to' a pollution discharge without naming the clause, describing it by a list of substances that does not exactly match the base exclusion's wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Whether it truly displaces the base pollution exclusion (c028), including its 'sudden and accidental' carve-back, is a whole-instrument question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exclusion is drafted for 'bodily injury' although this policy's insured harm is defined as 'personal injury' (c035), and the reference to 'Subparagraphs (a) and (d)(i))' is mis-set in the copy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The defined-term mismatch with c035 and c002 means the exclusion may not track the grant of coverage it is meant to cut back.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clean-up-cost limb is drafted in familiar ISO terms; 'in any way responding to' is broad but standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits with c094 and the Pollutants definition (c096); no competing provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any solid, liquid, gaseous or thermal irritant or contaminant' with an illustrative list is the classic general-versus-specific pollution definition that courts have repeatedly had to bound.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its breadth interacts with the coverage grant (c002) and with a hospital's ordinary operations, but no other clause directly contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Condition 1 (c044).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Payments will be considered past due if not received by the specified due dates' is definite, though it states no consequence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The consequence is supplied by the non-payment cancellation clause (c066), whose 10-day notice is in turn contradicted by c092.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'errors or omissions, malpractice or mistake of a professional nature ... in the conduct of the insured's business activities as a collection agency' is a compound but reasonably bounded formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 2 (c090) confines it to Med-Health Financial Services while the form speaks of 'the Insured' generally, so scope depends on reading the two together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat statement that no medical malpractice liability coverage is provided for statutory health care providers; the term 'medical malpractice liability' is not defined and may not match 'professional health care services' used elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps and partly conflicts with the Professional Services Exclusion (c082-c083), the professional liability aggregate in c084 and the contingency grant in c102.
